one_line: A 30-second launch ad for the 4th generation of Yoto kids' audio players: macro studio shots of coloured players and a hand pressing buttons, one kinetic text claim per shot, ending on a coral 'pre-order now' card.

hook.visual: Extreme close-up of a glossy green round button set into a mustard-yellow player body against a soft pastel backdrop, no text, then a cut to a front view of a white square player with a pixel-art sun and an 8:30 clock.
hook.on_screen_text: 0.0 s: none. 1.5 s: Yoto (Yoto). 3.0 and 4.5 s: Yoto 4th Generation (Yoto 4th Generation).
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Observed: a single saturated green shape fills the first frame with a soft shadow, an unexplained object before any logo. Inferred: the brand name appears at 1.5 s, so the viewer who recognises the product gets confirmation fast, and the 'new green button' becomes the thing to find out about.

beats.observed: Macro of a green button on a yellow player; no text.
beats.spoken: Whisper marks only (upbeat music); no speech.

beats.observed: Logo card over a white player showing a pixel sun and 8:30; then a white and a yellow mini player with two orange knobs, a pixel display and a green side button. The sampled frames show a new shot or text at every 1.5 s step.
beats.spoken: No speech transcribed (music marked only for 0 to 2.6 s).

beats.observed: A manicured finger presses the green button; text curves around it. Next a tight shot of the pixel display showing card art (a robot illustration) with text on top.
beats.on_screen_text: "new green button" (6.0 s, on a curve); "a shortcut to their favourite audio" (7.5 s)

beats.observed: Quick tactile macros, one claim each: a blue clip with a smiley face and braided cord; a finger on an orange knob; a pink player with orange knob under stretched text; a card with the word 'Music' slid toward a blue player; a blue player with a knob and speaker holes, no text; a white player with a green button under distorted text.
beats.on_screen_text: "amazing design" (9.0 s); "faster downloads" (10.5 s); "BIGGER memory" (12.0 s, stretched letters); "acoustically engineered sound" (13.5 s); none (15.0 s); "puddle proof*" (16.5 s, distorted letters, with an asterisk)

beats.observed: A pink player tumbling in frame under angled text; then a blurred orange glowing surface with a small logo, text on a diagonal.
beats.on_screen_text: "tough* tumble" (18.0 s, asterisk); "customisable night light" (19.5 s)

beats.observed: Two solid coral cards with white text, no product visible, the second in larger type.
beats.on_screen_text: "our best" (21.0 s); "our best Yoto yet" (22.5 s)

beats.observed: A blue player, then a macro of an orange knob on the blue body, no text; sampled frames at 24.0 and 25.5 s.
Yellow player with a pixel sun, 8:30 and the green side button in a clean studio shot (27.0 s), then a solid coral CTA card (28.5 s).

payoff: There is no single payoff. The viewer gets six or seven product claims between about 6 and 20 s, a 'our best Yoto yet' summary card at 21 to 23 s, and the offer 'pre-order now' at about 28.5 s.
cta: 'pre-order now' on a solid coral end card at about 28.5 s; the caption adds 'Pre-order now ... via the link in bio' and gives dispatch dates.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: parents who already use the product want to see what is new and tag a partner or relative as a gift or upgrade; the launch itself is the reason. Comments are 988 on 376,865 views (about 0.26%, roughly 17x the comment rate of the Busy Toddler pumpkin reel), but I cannot see the comments, so whether they are pre-order or price questions, a giveaway or other is unverified.
why_it_worked: 376,865 views is 23.1x the account median of 16,296: a launch moment on a small account with a product-loyal audience, which is a different mechanism from a generic idea reel (inferred).

Like rate of 1.96% is the highest of the three videos in this batch and well above the 0.3% paid threshold, so the interest looks real; observed: it is sound-off friendly because every claim is a 1 to 3 word kinetic caption on a new, tactile macro shot.

Observed: one claim per shot with a visible product detail each time (button, knob, card slot), plus a colour-block break (coral cards at 21 to 23 s) and a coral end card; the colourful physical-product feel is consistent from the first frame to the last.
paid_signal: unclear: the 1.96% like rate does not fit the low-like-rate paid pattern and no ad label is visible, but a 23.1x outlier on a product launch from a small account could have been boosted; nothing in the frames or meta.json shows it.

solo_route.how: 1) Shoot 6 to 8 phone macro shots (clip-on macro lens or the phone's macro mode) of a printed LumeBook sample on a plain, light backdrop with soft window light: cover title, a hand turning a page, the spine, the illustrated child's face on a spread. 2) In CapCut or Canva, give each shot one claim of 1 to 3 words using a kinetic text preset (curve, wobble, stretch); use only claims verified in the brand brief, and add an asterisk wherever a claim needs a qualifier, as Yoto does on 'puddle proof*' and 'tough*'. 3) Cut every 1 to 1.5 s, drop in 1 or 2 solid brand-colour cards with the line, and end on a solid CTA card ('free preview' in Hebrew). 4) Add an upbeat sound from the platform library and export at 20 to 25 s.
solo_route.needs: A few physical printed sample books, a clean backdrop and daylight; nothing else. The polish of the original (studio lighting, multiple coloured products, professional motion design) will be hard to match, and the 23x outlier relied on an existing audience wanting the product (inferred), not on the format.

lumebook_version.hook_he: הצצה ראשונה: ככה נראה הספר של הילד שלכם
lumebook_version.concept: A 20 to 25 s phone-macro first-look ad of the printed book: tactile close-ups (cover, page turn, paper edge, the illustrated child), one short kinetic Hebrew claim per shot, a solid-colour 'this is the one' card in the middle, and an end card pointing to the free preview. No speech needed, so it works sound-off.

evidence_notes: Observed: all shot descriptions and text come from frames sampled every 1.5 s, so the shot count and exact text timings are approximate and some brief texts or shots may fall between samples. Text is English only; the 'puddle proof*' overlay at 16.5 s is letter-distorted (confirmed in the single frame). Spoken: Whisper returns only '(upbeat music)' for 0 to 2.6 s and nothing afterwards, so there is no usable speech transcript and I infer the ad has no voiceover; I cannot describe the music or any sound effects beyond that tag. The caption mentions IP67, a night light, faster downloads and bigger memory, but the video itself only shows short text claims ('puddle proof*', 'tough* tumble'), so the IP67 rating is a caption claim, not shown in the video. No child appears; the hand in macro shots is unidentified. Brand-owned account (post owner Yoto); the polished studio production suggests an agency or in-house studio, which I cannot verify. Not a repost.
